chapter: Chicago, Ohio and Jelly Roll Morton
title: Jelly Roll's character and taking the road with him
summary: Thomas finds Jelly braggadocious but truthful, quotes his rule 'If you get lost, lay out,' and says he alone of the New York men went on the road.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: What kind of guy did you find him to be, Foots?
Very braggadocios. But the only thing about him bragging, everything he said was true!
He could play piano as good as anybody...

And he could sing. And you see, he didn't worry all day. He had one standard... In his first rehearsal with you... I'll always remember it. It sounded funny when I first heard it. He said, 'If you get lost, lay out.' And he explained what he meant. See, because if you get lost and try to catch up, you're going to be playing wrong notes. So just lay out until you know where to come in. Or if necessary, wait until the piece is over and then come in. But don't try to come in and catch up, because you'll be playing... He was a stickler on that. He said, 'If you get lost, lay out!' He didn't make no bones about it. He just said, 'Lay out.'

And I often wondered why he couldn't keep good musicians. Because he paid good money in those days; the
money in those days was good. But he just bragged so much. Now, I was about the only one in New York that went with him when he went on the road. Because he went on the road from the Rose Danceland.
Well, those guys were big-time cats in New York.
It's like I don't go on the road with the guys. I make the records, but by this time I've reached another standard.
Right, right. So I went on the road. I left my wife. She was pregnant with my daughter then. I took Delia(?) on the road with me for a while...
Delia was telling me about that the other night.
And I finally sent them to Ohio and let them stay... They didn't need to be out there on the road with me, all that scuffling and cold weather and cold joints.
